thread:
alex: quick sync — we should pick a default internal API shape for model routing/telemetry/quota enforcement. three options on the table, want opinions before i write an RFC.

alex: Option A: proto-first gRPC everywhere (typed, low-latency, native streaming). cheap to wire up service stubs, good for runtime perf. downsides: browser clients need grpc-web, and cross-language teams sometimes push back on proto ergonomics.

alex: Option B: REST JSON + gateway that translates to protos at edge. simpler for web/devex and dashboards, but we lose zero-copy proto efficiency and have to maintain gateway code and tests.

alex: Option C: hybrid — core internal services speak gRPC/proto; edge/gateway exposes JSON and handles schema translation, header propagation, quota tagging, and tracing. promotes typed core + dev-friendly edges.

priya: +1 for C. we get typed contracts where it matters and keep product teams happy. main worry: who owns the gateway translation tests and contract updates?

marco: C seems pragmatic. for rollouts we need clear compatibility rules: additive fields ok, enum deprecations require migration plan. also need automated CI that validates proto->json roundtrip.

sam: quick perf note: gRPC lets us preserve streaming KV-cache semantics for long-lived model sessions. gateway introduces a 1 hop and potential buffering which hurts tail latency. if latency SLOs are strict, prefer proto in-path.

jun: telemetry + quotas: we should standardize headers for tenant-id, route, model-version, and chargeable_tokens. gateway must copy those 1:1. otherwise console dashboards will show garbage.

erin: UX for rollouts: console should show per-model rollout % + fallbacks (e.g., if dedicated capacity exhausted, fallback to lower-cost variant). regardless of transport, routing policy needs the same config surface.

priya: re: quotas — enforcement point matters. pushing enforcement to gateway simplifies accounting but creates single choke. enforcement at service is more robust but duplicates logic. thoughts?

marco: split responsibility: gateway tags and approximate-quotas (fast path), authoritative enforcement at model-service. gateway can be a fast-reject to save cycles but service does final check.

alex: digging into proto evolution: proto-first gives us a single source of truth for types and generated clients. sample proto snippet:```proto
service ModelRouter {
  rpc Route(RouteRequest) returns (RouteResponse) {}
}
message RouteRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  string model = 2;
  map<string,string> meta = 3;
}
```

alex: gateway JSON example for product teams:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/route -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"tenant_id":"acme","model":"gpt-4x","meta":{"prompt_type":"assist"}}'
```

sam: note to infra: we need to maintain header propagation for tracing (x-request-id, x-b3-*, traceparent) and ensure correlation id flows from gateway -> model service -> runtime.

jun: dashboard needs: per-route latency P50/P95/P99, token consumption, per-tenant rejection rates, and canary signal heatmap. add a 'schema-mismatch' alert if gateway translation drops fields.

erin: rollout UX: console should let PMs create a canary with percentage and conditional filters (region, tenant tier). tie metrics to canary predicates (latency, error-rate, quality evals).

priya: testing matrix: proto lint, compatibility check, gateway JSON roundtrip, integration e2e with canary traffic generator. owner: eng-platform + infra-test.

marco: one more thing — client codegen. if we go proto-first we should publish generated SDKs (python/node/go) and a small JS shim for browsers (grpc-web + fetch fallback). keeps DX consistent.

alex: ok consensus? i'm leaning to Option C with the split quota enforcement and the testing/SDK commitments. want a thumbs-up and volunteers for the RFC: owner + reviewers.

sam: 👍 for C, volunteer to own perf/latency criteria and streaming tests.

priya: 👍 i'll own gateway translation tests and contract CI.

marco: 👍 i'll own proto compatibility checker and codegen pipeline.

jun: i'll pair with sam on quota metric definitions.

deploy-bot: Canary created: model-routing-gateway-v1 -> 5% traffic (triggered by alex) :rocket:

erin: thanks — i'll draft the console UX mockups and link in the RFC.

alex: awesome, i'll write RFC draft and tag owners. i want the RFC up by EOD tomorrow. :+1:
